headline: Math benchmarks are nearly exhausted while real-world agent work lags behind
outlook: Math is where the field has moved fastest: the past twelve months closed 95% of the remaining headroom, FrontierMath crossed 90% in September, and GPT-6.1 Sol has now posted 100% on FrontierMath Tier 4. Agents and real work are moving much more slowly, closing only 32% of their headroom, with the Remote Labor Index at 20.8% and OSWorld 2 at 31.4%; on current trends neither reaches 90% before mid-2027 at the earliest. The bridge between those two pictures is task length: Claude Mythos Preview now handles tasks of about 17.4 hours, and with that horizon doubling roughly every 4.2 months, the trend points to full work-week tasks around December, though the likely range runs into August 2027. Not everything is on schedule, since sub-cent pricing for GPQA-level models, Terminal-Bench and GeoBench have all fallen behind their fitted dates. The site's past ranges caught the real date only 59% of the time, so the coming year may bring longer autonomous work, but the timing of each step is far from certain.
